messages:
Zoe Martin: Hi all! New hire question from week 1 — I uploaded all Workday paperwork but still seeing a note that benefits are "pending". When will my medical/dental/vision kick in? Also I bought a USB-C dock for $59.99 to connect at home, is that reimbursable? Lastly, how do holidays get pro-rated for mid-year starts?

Lina Patel (People Ops): welcome Zoe! :wave: Short answers: 1) Benefits: enrollment needs to be completed in the benefits portal within 30 days of start. Typical effective date is the first of the month following 30 days after your start date. 2) Reimbursements: Submit the receipt via Spendesk and tag your manager for approval. <$75 is fine to submit after purchase; >$250 needs pre-approval. 3) Holidays: company holidays are pro-rated in your first calendar year based on hire date. PTO accrual starts day 1 but some teams require 90 days before taking extended time — check your offer letter or ask your manager.

Zoe Martin: Thanks Lina — I started 2024-07-18 so that means coverage starts 2024-09-01, right? (first of the month after 30 days)

Benefits-Bot: Enrollment status: pending for Zoe Martin. Vendor invite sent to zoe.martin@redwood.com on 2024-07-18. Reminder email queued for 2024-07-20.

Lina Patel: Quick calc: start 07/18 -> 30 days ends 08/17 -> coverage effective 09/01. So yes, 09/01 is expected. If you need immediate care before then see the carrier's urgent care policy or we can open an exception for emergencies.

Zoe Martin: Got it, that's helpful. For Spendesk: can I submit a photo of the receipt? Also do I need to include a short justification?

Harper Lee (Engineering Manager): hi Zoe — yes, photo or PDF is fine. Include a short note like "home setup: USB-C dock" and tag me (harper.lee) as approver. If IT has stock and you prefer that route, ping eng-it.

Zoe Martin: Cool. One more weird payroll thing — my offer said biweekly pay, but I saw a message about a retro starter payment in case of cutoffs. How does that work? I want to make sure I don't go a month without pay.

Lina Patel: payroll outline: we run biweekly Fridays. Cutoff is Tuesday 11:59pm PT. New hires who complete payroll forms after cutoff may see their first pay on the next cycle; we can issue a retro starter payment in the following run if needed. If you're concerned, DM payroll@redwood with your start date and confirmation you uploaded direct deposit and SSN and we can confirm the expected first pay date.

Zoe Martin: I uploaded direct deposit yesterday. I'll DM payroll now. Also curious about adding my partner as a dependent — do we need marriage docs? We're domestic partners, not married yet.

Lina Patel: For domestic partners we need a completed domestic partner affidavit (uploaded with benefits enrollment) and SSN + DOB for the dependent. The portal will prompt you for documents. Add them within 30 days of hire to avoid waiting for a qualifying life event.

Marcus Holt (Finance): FYI for receipts: Spendesk requires an itemized merchant receipt and proof of payment. Personal/combined receipts sometimes need an extra note. For small office items like your dock, tag it as "home office" and include manager approval.

Zoe Martin: Thanks Marcus — the receipt is a card charge only, merchant provided an itemized email. I'll attach both. One last question — our handbook mentions voluntary pre-tax commuter benefits. Do new hires get those immediately or only after 30 days?

Lina Patel: commuter benefits are available after benefits enrollment is active. You can elect commuter in the portal once your benefits take effect. If you need a payroll deduction earlier, it's not possible until enrollment is active.

Zoe Martin: Thanks everyone. Submitting Spendesk now and I'll watch for the BeneCorp invite. Appreciate the quick help! :smile:
